items.title: Delayed Jobs aren't run after cycling Redis
items.body:
OS: Ubuntu 20.04
Python: 3.11
Dramatiq: 1.14.0
Redis: "redis:6.2-alpine" Docker image

I created an actor `args` that simply takes an arg and prints it, then ran the following tests:

### Test 1

Tried:  Enqueue job with small delay using `send_with_options(delay=)`.
Result:  Ran successfully after the delay.

### Test 2

Tried:  Enqueue job with small delay, then quickly kill Dramatiq and restart it.
Result:  Still ran job successfully at the appropriate time.

### Test 3

Tried:  Enqueue job with small delay, then quickly kill Redis and restart it.
Result:  Job never runs.  (I can still see the message in Redis key `dramatiq:default.DQ.msgs`.)

When I killed Redis, the worker pool spit out connection errors, but then reconnected.  I tested that by submitting a normal job (not delayed) shortly after, and it ran successfully - proving the workers did re-connect to Redis after Redis came back up.

items.title: Message duplication under high load of a worker with RabbitMQ broker
items.body:
# Issues

When launching CPU intensive tasks from the delayed queue with a high amount of threads 
dramatiq raises 
`pika.exceptions.ConnectionWrongStateError: BlockingConnection.add_callback_threadsafe() called on closed or closing connection.`
errors and duplicates tasks across the queues. 

## What OS are you using?

Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS

## What version of Dramatiq are you using?

1.12.1

## What did you do?

Created a file called example.py and loaded the messages in the queue:
`python3 example.py` 

```python3
import dramatiq
import time


@dramatiq.actor
def slow_thing():
    start_t = time.monotonic()
    while time.monotonic() - start_t < 100:
        2 * 2

def example():
    delay = 15000
    for i in range(100):
        delay += 1000
        slow_thing.send_with_options(delay=delay)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    example()
```
Then I launched the worker with a high amount of threads.
`dramatiq example --threads=40 --processes=1`

The notebook is based around a Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10610U.
The issue does  depend on the right load. So you may need to play
a little bit with the thread count to get the same results.

## What did you expect would happen?

I expected to see the messages being moved from the delayed queue to the normal queue:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5213399/147590448-e34e7265-889a-4655-8f33-f42b5d772c82.png)

During the process I expect both totals to be 100 tasks.
At the end I expect something like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5213399/147590563-e7456d4b-a39a-4bd9-9e81-e49e55a01c15.png)

(1 item is already processed after 100 seconds)

This is an example made with `dramatiq example --threads=1 --processes=1`.

## What happened?

Initially it all started OK:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5213399/147590758-592d9169-ff9f-462d-a64f-dbb832e5cc43.png)

However once all threads start to take more work the totals become out of balance: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5213399/147590898-22f71279-07a2-47c0-9dec-eb324cebc4b4.png)

Some time later I see this message in my terminal:

```
[2021-12-28 18:17:55,826] [PID 175469] [Thread-3] [dramatiq.brokers.rabbitmq._RabbitmqConsumer] [ERROR] Failed to wait for all callbacks to complete.  This can happen when the RabbitMQ server is suddenly restarted.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/x/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/dramatiq-issue-example-Abb_BWZr-py3.8/lib/python3.8/site-packages/dramatiq/brokers/rabbitmq.py", line 542, in close
    self.connection.add_callback_threadsafe(all_callbacks_handled.set)
  File "/home/x/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/dramatiq-issue-example-Abb_BWZr-py3.8/lib/python3.8/site-packages/pika/adapters/blocking_connection.py", line 742, in add_callback_threadsafe
    raise exceptions.ConnectionWrongStateError(
pika.exceptions.ConnectionWrongStateError: BlockingConnection.add_callback_threadsafe() called on closed or closing connection.
```

When I now kill the dramatiq worker I'm left in this state:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5213399/147591024-50c0fab8-d15d-4e47-bd10-81549e3faae4.png)

When I launch/stop/lauch the worker a few times for the problem becomes even bigger. We now have more than twice the amount of messages that we originally created.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5213399/147591496-86c862fd-de23-423c-a8c2-a254e0c93b88.png)

## Related resources

Issue created after the discussion of the default thread count for dramatiq_django:
https://github.com/Bogdanp/django_dramatiq/issues/115

items.title: Some AMQP connections are closed due to missed heartbeats after dramatiq boot
items.body:
# Issues
After dramatiq cli boots,some amqp connections are getting closed from rabbitmq couple of seconds after, depending on the heartbeat settings.
```
rabbitmq_1        | 2020-06-24 11:53:50.358 [error] <0.3580.0> closing AMQP connection <0.3580.0> (172.19.0.5:39108 -> 172.19.0.9:5672):
rabbitmq_1        | missed heartbeats from client, timeout: 5s
```
I believe they are as many as the queues declared * number of worker processes

I think they are the connections used by the `RabbitmqBroker` used to declare queues,enqueuing etc. because the connections setup by ` _RabbitmqConsumer` in the consumer threads are kept alive.

I believe the same may also happen later because broker.connection is also used for enqueuing delayed messages, retries etc. given they will stay stale for too long?

## What OS are you using?

Linux Mint 18 64-bit 4.4.0-174-generic


## What did you expect would happen?
What if the the worker was closing the connections that doesn't intend to keep alive to avoid them being closed from the rabbitmq's side if possible? Opening and closing connections would have a performance impact of course but how much would that be?  Otherwise what would be the impact of disabling heartbeats for those connections(or using a much larger value) and keeping them enabled only for consumer connections?

Those messages on the rabbitmq's side are a bit distracting / indicating that something bad happened, especially while troubleshooting other issues.
